**AI 380: Human-AI Interaction**

Your assistant works in `rasa inspect`. Now make it reachable by other people.

- **Free:** GitHub Codespaces, Azure for Students
- **Paid:** DigitalOcean
- **Shared:** the same preparation for all three

## 🎯 Goals for this session

By the end you can:

1. Explain what **every** deployment needs before you pick a host.
2. Compare the three options by cost, uptime, and effort.
3. Choose one and justify it.
4. Start deploying your own assistant by following its **basic steps**.

> Detailed walkthroughs exist for Azure and Codespaces. This deck is the map.

## 🗺️ Three options at a glance

| | **GitHub Codespaces** | **Azure VM** | **DigitalOcean Droplet** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cost | Free allowance | Student credit | Paid (monthly) |
| Always on | No (idle stop) | Yes | Yes |
| Public URL for others | Not for long | Yes | Yes |
| Free HTTPS name | Yes (forwarded port) | Yes (`cloudapp.azure.com`) | No (bring a domain) |
| Setup effort | Lowest | Highest | Medium |
| Best for | Labs, demos, testing | Graded, free, online | Simple, reliable, paid |

::: {.notes}
Prices and allowances change. Have students check the official pages before the session.
:::

## ① Common pre-deployment {.section-slide background-color="#2f4f9d"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Part 1 · Do this before choosing a host
:::

**Docker → GitHub → front end → secrets → protection**

## 📋 Pre-deployment checklist

| Step | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Finish and test with `rasa train` + `rasa inspect` | Never debug on a server what you can debug locally |
| 2 | Note `rasa --version` | Server must run the **same** version |
| 3 | Put keys in **environment variables** | No secrets in files or git |
| 4 | Containerize: official Rasa image + Compose | Same run command everywhere |
| 5 | Push to **GitHub** (without secrets or `models/`) | Every host pulls from here |
| 6 | Decide the **front end**: Inspector or `webchat.html` | Decides what users open |
| 7 | Plan **protection**: HTTPS + password | Your LLM key and user logs are at stake |

## 🐳 Step 4 · Docker, the minimal way

You do **not** need your own Dockerfile. Use Rasa's official image and mount your project:

```yaml
services:
  assistant:
    image: <official rasa-pro image>:<your tested version>
    command: ["run", "--inspect"]
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - ..:/app
```

- Actions run inside Rasa, so there is no action server.
- Train once on the server: `docker compose run --rm assistant train`.
- A reverse proxy (Caddy) adds HTTPS and a password. See the Azure deck for the full files.

## 🐙 Step 5 · GitHub, what goes in and out

| Commit | Never commit |
|---|---|
| `actions/`, `data/`, `domain.yml`, `config.yml` | `.env` (license, LLM key, password hash) |
| `endpoints.yml`, `credentials.yml` | `models/`, `.rasa/` |
| `deploy/` (Compose, Caddyfile, `.env.example`) | `lesson_log.jsonl` (user IDs and replies) |
| `.gitignore` | Any API key, ever |

Private repo on a server? Give that one server a **read-only deploy key**.

## 🖼️ Step 6 · Front end: Inspector or webchat.html?

| | **Rasa Inspector** | **Custom `webchat.html`** |
|---|---|---|
| How | `rasa run --inspect` | A small page that calls Rasa's REST channel |
| Effort | None | Write and host one HTML file |
| Shows | Chat, Flow, History, Memory | Only what **you** render |
| Audience | You, classmates, grader | Real end users |
| Design control | None | Full (large text, buttons, highlights) |

> **Not required.** Use the Inspector to deploy. Build `webchat.html` when the *interface* is part of what you are demonstrating.

## 💬 What `webchat.html` does

1. Sends the user's text to `POST /webhooks/rest/webhook` (needs `rest:` in `credentials.yml`).
2. Reads the JSON reply: `text`, `buttons`, and `custom` (your highlight payload).
3. **Renders** text and buttons in your own style.
4. Sends a button's `payload` back as the next message.

This is where the App Coach **highlight** idea becomes visible: Rasa sends `{"highlight": "add_reminder_button"}`; your page draws the ring.

## 💻 A minimal `webchat.html`

```html
<div id="log"></div>
<input id="msg"><button id="go">Send</button>
<script>
const log = document.getElementById("log");
const add = (t) => { const p = document.createElement("p"); p.textContent = t; log.append(p); };
async function send(text, label = text) {
  add("You: " + label);
  const r = await fetch("/webhooks/rest/webhook", { method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ sender: "web-user-1", message: text }) });
  for (const m of await r.json()) {
    if (m.text) add("Coach: " + m.text);
    for (const b of m.buttons || []) {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = b.title; btn.onclick = () => send(b.payload, b.title);
      log.append(btn);
    }
    if (m.custom?.highlight) add("[highlight: " + m.custom.highlight + "]");
  }
}
document.getElementById("go").onclick = () => send(msg.value);
</script>
```

## 🔌 Hosting `webchat.html`

| Pattern | How | Watch out |
|---|---|---|
| **Same origin** (preferred) | Caddy serves the page and proxies `/webhooks/*` to Rasa | No CORS setup; one HTTPS address |
| **Separate host** | Page on GitHub Pages, Rasa elsewhere | Rasa must allow that origin (`--cors`); never use `*` on a public server |

- The page uses `textContent`, not `innerHTML`, so a bot or user message cannot inject HTML.
- The password gate protects the page **and** the API. A public end-user page needs a different protection plan.

::: {.notes}
Treat the Caddy pattern as a sketch to test: handle /webhooks/* with reverse_proxy, and serve the page with file_server from a mounted folder.
:::

## 🔐 Step 7 · Secrets and protection

- **Secrets:** license, LLM key, password hash live in `.env` or the host's secret store.
- **HTTPS:** microphone access needs it; Caddy gets certificates automatically.
- **Password:** a login before any request reaches Rasa.
- **Ports:** only 80/443 public. Never publish Rasa's 5005.
- **Logs:** `lesson_log.jsonl` has user IDs. Know who can read it and delete it when done.

> An open Rasa URL lets strangers spend your LLM key.

## ✅ Pre-deployment checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
**Before you pick a host, you can say yes to all of these:**

- Works in `rasa inspect`, and I know my Rasa version
- Keys are in environment variables
- Project is on GitHub without `.env`, `models/`, or the log
- I chose Inspector or `webchat.html`
- I know how I will add HTTPS and a password
:::

## ② The three options {.section-slide background-color="#263b3e"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Part 2 · Basic steps for each
:::

**Free · Free · Paid**

## 🧑‍💻 Option A · GitHub Codespaces

**What it is:** a cloud dev machine in your browser, tied to your repo.

| Strength | Limit |
|---|---|
| No server to manage; Docker ready | Stops after about 30 idle minutes |
| HTTPS URL comes from port forwarding | Free hours are limited (roughly 120 core hours a month) |
| Everyone gets the same environment | Not an always-on site |

**Best for:** class labs, demos, and testing before a real deploy.

## 🧑‍💻 Codespaces · Basic steps

1. Repo → **Code → Codespaces → Create codespace**.
2. Add `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (Python, Docker-in-Docker, ports 5005 and 8000).
3. Add `RASA_LICENSE` and your LLM key as **Codespaces secrets**.
4. Train and run: `rasa train`, then `rasa inspect` (or the Compose command).
5. In the **Ports** tab, open the forwarded **5005** URL.
6. **Stop** the codespace when done.

Keep Rasa's port **Private**. Use a 4-core machine for training.

## ☁️ Option B · Azure VM

**What it is:** a Linux VM you control, paid from **student credit**.

| Strength | Limit |
|---|---|
| Free for students (credit, no card) | Most steps to set up |
| Always on, with a free `cloudapp.azure.com` name | A 4 GB VM uses credit, not the free VM allowance |
| Good fit for a graded, public URL | Billing continues until you **deallocate** |

**Best for:** a free, always-on deployment you can submit.

## ☁️ Azure · Basic steps

1. Create the account and a **5 USD budget alert**.
2. Cloud Shell: create a resource group and a 4 GB Ubuntu VM with a DNS label.
3. Open ports **80** and **443**.
4. SSH in and install Docker.
5. Clone the repo, create `deploy/.env`, run `docker compose run --rm assistant train`.
6. `docker compose up -d`, then open your `https://` address.
7. Deallocate when idle; delete the resource group at the end.

## 🌊 Option C · DigitalOcean

**What it is:** a simple paid cloud server (a **Droplet**).

| Strength | Limit |
|---|---|
| Clean interface and flat, predictable pricing | Costs money from the first hour |
| Docker-ready images and quick setup | No free HTTPS hostname: bring a domain |
| Always on | Bill continues until you **destroy** the Droplet |

**Best for:** the simplest reliable paid option, or when you outgrow free credit.

::: {.notes}
Check current pricing and any student or promotional credit (for example through the GitHub Student Developer Pack) before the session.
:::

## 🌊 DigitalOcean · Basic steps

1. Create an account and add a payment method (or apply credit).
2. Create a **Droplet**: Ubuntu, about 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM, with your **SSH key**.
3. Add a **firewall** allowing 22, 80, 443.
4. Point a domain's **A record** at the Droplet's IP.
5. SSH in, install Docker, clone the repo, create `deploy/.env` with that domain.
6. Train, then `docker compose up -d`.
7. When finished, **destroy** the Droplet.

## 🌐 The domain question

Azure gives a free name. DigitalOcean does not.

| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| Your own domain | Add an A record to the server IP. Cleanest |
| A wildcard-DNS service that maps an IP to a name | Free and quick for a class demo, but shared certificate limits may bite; verify it works |

HTTPS needs a **name**, not a bare IP address.

## ⚖️ Compare, side by side

| Question | Codespaces | Azure | DigitalOcean |
|---|---|---|---|
| Money | Free quota | Student credit | Monthly bill |
| Someone else can visit tomorrow | No | Yes | Yes |
| Caddy/HTTPS to configure | No | Yes | Yes |
| Memory for Rasa Pro | Pick 4-core | Pick 4 GB VM | Pick 4 GB Droplet |
| Risk if you forget it | Hours used up | Credit spent | **Money spent** |
| Typical lab effort | Short | Longest | Medium |

## 🧭 How to choose

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["Do others need to visit<br/>your URL after class?"] -->|No| B["🧑‍💻 Codespaces"]
    A -->|Yes| C["Free required?"]
    C -->|Yes| D["☁️ Azure for Students"]
    C -->|No| E["Want the simplest<br/>always-on server?"]
    E -->|Yes| F["🌊 DigitalOcean"]
    E -->|No| D
```

## 💡 Recommendations and why

| Situation | Choose | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| First try, class lab, debugging | **Codespaces** | Nothing to provision; same environment for everyone; free |
| Graded project that must stay online, no budget | **Azure** | Free credit, always on, free HTTPS hostname |
| Reliable demo, willing to pay, want less friction | **DigitalOcean** | Simpler interface and pricing; you handle the domain |
| Not sure | **Codespaces first, then Azure** | Learn the pieces cheaply, then deploy for real |

## 🧪 Class activity

1. **Choose** one option.
2. **Finish pre-deployment** (the checklist) and show your repo.
3. **Deploy** using that option's basic steps and the detailed deck.
4. **Verify**: the Inspector (or `webchat.html`) works at your URL and the log has events.
5. **Clean up**: stop, deallocate, or destroy.

Pairs are fine. Help classmates on **other** options when you finish.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Done when:** you completed a guided lesson at your own URL and can name one thing that went wrong.
:::

## 🧯 Common problems on every host

| Symptom | Likely cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| License or LLM error at startup | Missing or misnamed variable → check `.env` / secrets |
| "No model found" | Not trained on the server → run `train` |
| Version warning | Image tag differs from yours → align and retrain |
| Page loads but chat cannot connect | Wrong public URL, or CORS → use the https address; same origin |
| Certificate fails | Port 80 blocked or wrong domain → open ports, check `DOMAIN` |
| Out of memory | Machine too small → 4 GB or larger |
| Works locally, not remotely | Secret or file missing in git → compare with `.gitignore` |

## 💸 Cost and safety, every time

- Set a **budget alert** before creating anything.
- **Stop** (Codespaces), **deallocate** (Azure), or **destroy** (DigitalOcean) when you finish.
- Never leave Rasa's port open to the internet.
- Never post a URL **and** its password together.
- Delete `lesson_log.jsonl` when the course ends.

> Most surprise bills come from something left running.

## 💭 Discussion

1. Which option would you pick for a real older-adult user, and why?
2. The Inspector exposes History and Memory. Should end users see that? What does `webchat.html` let you hide or show?
3. A password protects your LLM key. What other risks come with a public coach?
4. If your host disappears tomorrow, how fast can you redeploy? What does that say about your repo?
5. Which step would you automate first?

## 🏁 Wrap-up

**Prepare once, deploy anywhere.**

- The **pre-deployment** work is the same for every host.
- **Codespaces** to learn, **Azure** to stay free and online, **DigitalOcean** when you want simple and are willing to pay.
- Protect the URL, watch the bill, and shut things down.

> A deployed assistant is one you can update, protect, and shut down.
